question.text: National Savings Certificates (NSC VIII issue) have a tenor of 5 years with interest compounded annually. Which of the following entities is NOT eligible to purchase NSCs?

answer.text: Resident individual on behalf of a minor
Two joint holders on either-or-survivor basis

explanation.text: The Logic: NRIs, HUFs, companies, trusts, societies, and other institutions are not allowed to purchase NSCs. Only resident individuals can buy — on their own account, on behalf of a minor, or jointly with up to two joint holders. The Trap: Joint holding by two individuals is allowed, so that option may look like a restriction but is in fact permitted. Note: NSC's accrued interest is treated as reinvested (other than the final year's interest), keeping the reinvested amount eligible for Section 80C benefit during the tenor.
